name: Kettlebell deadlift
steps: Stand with feet about hip-width apart, the bell on the floor between your mid-feet.
Push your hips back and let your knees bend a little until you can grip the handle with both hands.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears and make your back flat and long.
Take a breath, brace your stomach, and stand up tall by driving your feet into the floor.
Finish standing straight with glutes squeezed, then push your hips back to lower the bell to the floor.
formCues: Stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach the bell.
Squatting the weight up instead of hinging at the hips.
Leaning back at the top instead of standing straight.
Letting the bell drift forward, away from the body.
videoTitle: Kettlebell Deadlift to Kettlebell Swing | StrongFirst

name: Goblet squat
steps: Hold the bell by the horns (sides of the handle) close to your chest, elbows pointing down.
Stand with feet a little wider than your hips, toes turned slightly out.
Sit down between your heels, keeping your chest up and the bell close.
Go as low as you can while your back stays flat and heels stay down.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
formCues: Elbows inside the knees at the bottom.
Chest tall, bell glued to your chest.
commonMistakes: Heels lifting off the floor.
Knees caving inward.
Letting the bell pull the chest forward.
Cutting depth short on every rep.
videoTitle: Goblet Squat | Onnit Academy (Short)

name: Prying goblet squat
steps: Hold the bell by the horns at your chest and squat down to the bottom of a goblet squat.
Rest your elbows against the inside of your knees.
Gently push your knees out with your elbows and shift your weight side to side.
Breathe slowly and relax into the bottom position for a few seconds.
Stand up tall. That is one rep.
formCues: Relax at the bottom and breathe.
Use the elbows to open the hips.
commonMistakes: Rushing through it like a working squat.
Rounding the back to get lower.
videoTitle: Kettlebell Prying Goblet Squat | StrongFirst

name: Two-hand swing
steps: Set the bell about a foot in front of you. Hinge back and grip the handle with both hands, tilting the bell toward you.
Hike the bell back between your legs like a football snap, high up near your zipper.
Snap your hips forward and stand up tall so the bell floats up to chest height. Your arms just guide it.
Let the bell fall; wait until your forearms touch your thighs, then hinge and let it swing back through.
To finish, hike it back one last time and park it on the floor in front of you.
formCues: It's a hip snap, not an arm lift.
Hike it high between the legs.
Stand tall like a plank at the top.
Wait for the bell before you hinge.
commonMistakes: Squatting the swing instead of hinging.
Lifting the bell with the arms or shoulders.
Leaning back at the top.
Letting the bell swing low toward the knees on the backswing.
Hinging too early so the bell drags you forward.
videoTitle: Kettlebell Swing | Onnit (Juan Leija)

name: One-arm swing
steps: Set up like a two-hand swing, but grip the handle with one hand. The free arm can hang at your side.
Hike the bell back high between your legs.
Snap the hips forward and stand tall so the bell floats to chest height.
Keep the working shoulder packed down, and don't let the bell twist your torso.
Hike it back and park it before switching hands.
formCues: Square hips and shoulders, don't twist.
commonMistakes: Rotating the torso to follow the bell.
Shrugging the working shoulder up.
Switching hands without control.
videoTitle: One Arm Kettlebell Swing by Pavel Tsatsouline

name: Single-arm press
steps: Clean or lift the bell to the rack position: handle in your palm, bell resting on the outside of your forearm, elbow tucked to your ribs.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach so you're solid from feet to shoulders.
Press the bell straight up until your arm is locked out next to your ear, with your wrist straight.
Lower it under control back to the rack.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Straight wrist, knuckles to the ceiling.
Bicep by the ear at the top.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to push the bell up.
Bent wrist letting the bell flop back.
Elbow flaring out wide in the rack.
videoTitle: Single Arm Kettlebell Press Exercise | Onnit Tutorial

name: Single-arm row
steps: Stagger your stance and hinge forward, with your free hand on your thigh or a bench for support.
Let the bell hang from the working arm under your shoulder.
Pull the bell toward your hip, driving the elbow back.
Pause, then lower it under control until your arm is straight.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to swing the bell up.
Rounding the back.
Shrugging instead of pulling with the back.
videoTitle: Single-Arm Bent Kettlebell Row Exercise | Onnit Tutorial

name: Kettlebell windmill
steps: Press or hold a light bell overhead with one arm locked out. Beginners can do it with no bell.
Turn both feet about 45° away from the bell side.
Keep your eyes on the bell and push your hip out toward the bell side.
Hinge sideways and slide your free hand down the inside of your front leg toward the floor.
Go only as far as your back stays long, then stand back up by driving the hip back under you.
formCues: Eyes on the bell the whole time.
Push the hip out, then hinge.
Overhead arm stays locked and vertical.
commonMistakes: Bending the overhead elbow.
Rounding the back to reach the floor.
Looking away from the bell.
videoTitle: Kettlebell Windmill | Onnit Academy

name: Chin-up
steps: Grip the bar with palms facing you, hands shoulder-width apart.
Hang with arms straight, then pull your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
Lower yourself under control until your arms are straight again.
commonMistakes: Kicking or swinging for momentum.
Half reps without straightening the arms.
Reaching the chin up instead of pulling the body up.
videoTitle: Correct vs Incorrect Chin Up | Athlean-X

name: Dead hang
steps: Grip a pull-up bar with both hands, about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms.
Keep your shoulders gently engaged, not shrugged all the way up to your ears.
Breathe and hold as long as you can with good grip, then step down.
commonMistakes: Dropping off without control.
Holding your breath.

name: Dip
steps: Grip the parallel bars and press up so your arms are straight, shoulders down.
Lean slightly forward and lower yourself by bending your elbows.
Go down until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or as deep as your shoulders are comfortable.
Press back up to straight arms.
commonMistakes: Sinking too deep and straining the shoulders.
Shrugging at the bottom.
Bouncing out of the bottom.
videoTitle: Are You Doing Dips Properly? (AVOID MISTAKES!) | Athlean-X

name: Bench dip
steps: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench or chair and put your hands next to your hips, fingers forward.
Slide your hips off the edge, feet on the floor with knees bent.
Bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor.
Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, then press back up.
commonMistakes: Going too deep and rolling the shoulders forward.
Letting the elbows flare out.
videoTitle: How to do a Bench Dip | Proper Form & Technique | NASM

name: Push-up
steps: Place your hands a little wider than your shoulders and step back into a straight plank.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach.
Lower your chest toward the floor with elbows at about 45° from your body.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight.
Make it easier with hands on a bench or knees down.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips.
Elbows flared straight out.
Partial range of motion.
videoTitle: How to do a Push-Up | Proper Form & Technique | NASM

name: Kettlebell overhead squat
steps: Press one bell overhead and lock the arm out, bicep by your ear.
Keep your eyes on the bell or straight ahead and your ribs down.
Squat down while the overhead arm stays locked and vertical.
Go as low as your arm stays straight and your back stays flat.
Stand back up, then lower the bell to the rack to switch sides between sets.
formCues: Arm locked and stacked over the shoulder.
Squat straight down between the heels.
commonMistakes: Letting the overhead arm drift forward.
Bending the elbow.
Squatting deeper than the shoulder mobility allows.
videoTitle: Single Arm Overhead Kettlebell Squat - OPEX Exercise Library

name: Turkish get-up
steps: Lie on your back. Bring the bell to your chest with both hands, then press it up with one arm. Bend the knee on the same side, foot flat.
Roll to the opposite elbow, then push up to your hand, keeping eyes on the bell.
Lift your hips high into a bridge.
Sweep the straight leg under you to a kneeling position.
Straighten your torso to tall kneeling, turn the back foot, and stand up.
Reverse every step slowly to lie back down. That's one rep.
Beginner option: do it with no bell, or balance a shoe on your fist.
formCues: Eyes on the bell until you're kneeling.
Arm locked and vertical the whole time.
Move slowly, one position at a time.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the positions.
Bending the arm holding the bell.
Hips too low in the bridge, so the leg can't sweep through.
videoTitle: Turkish Get-Up Basics | StrongFirst (Lance Coffel & Zar Horton)

name: Halo
steps: Hold a light bell upside down by the horns in front of your chest.
Circle it around your head, close to your neck, keeping your stomach tight.
Return to the front. That's one rep.
Do all reps in one direction, then switch directions.
formCues: Stay tall and keep your ribs down.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back.
Making huge circles far from the head.
videoTitle: Kettlebell Halo | StrongFirst

name: Hip bridge
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Press through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
Hold for a second at the top with a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lower slowly.
formCues: Squeeze your glutes, don't arch your back.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back instead of using the glutes.
Feet too far from the hips.
videoTitle: Glute Bridge: Proper Form (NASM trainer)

name: Suitcase carry
steps: Deadlift the bell up with one hand, holding it at your side like a suitcase.
Stand perfectly tall, without leaning toward or away from the bell.
Walk slowly with small, controlled steps.
Set it down with a good hinge, then switch hands.
commonMistakes: Leaning to one side.
Letting the bell bang against the leg.
Rushing the steps.
videoTitle: Kettlebell Kings Presents: Kettlebell Suitcase Carries

name: Plank
steps: Place your forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body is a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes, brace your stomach, and breathe.
Hold for the time, then lower your knees.
formCues: Straight line from head to heels.
commonMistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor.
Hips piked up high.
Holding your breath.
videoTitle: How to do a Plank | Proper Form & Technique | NASM

name: Hip circles
steps: Stand with hands on your hips, feet shoulder-width apart.
Make big slow circles with your hips.
Switch directions halfway through.
commonMistakes: Moving too fast.
Tiny circles.

name: Cat-cow
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Breathe in and let your belly drop while you look up (cow).
Breathe out and round your back toward the ceiling while you tuck your chin (cat).
Move slowly between the two positions.
formCues: Move one segment of the spine at a time.
commonMistakes: Rushing.
Only moving the neck.
videoTitle: How to Do Cat-Cow Stretch With Micki Duran | Yoga52

name: World's greatest stretch
steps: Step into a long lunge with your right foot forward and put your left hand on the floor.
Drop your right elbow toward the inside of your right foot.
Rotate and reach your right arm up to the ceiling, following it with your eyes.
Return your hand to the floor, step back, and switch sides.
formCues: Back knee off the floor if you can.
commonMistakes: Short lunge stance.
Forcing the elbow to the floor.
videoTitle: The World's Greatest Stretch (Mobility Exercise) by Squat University

name: Walk
steps: Walk at an easy, conversational pace.
Outside is best. Leave the phone in your pocket if you can.
formCues: Easy pace, nose breathing if you can.
commonMistakes: Turning a recovery walk into a hard workout.

name: Bodyweight squat
steps: Stand with feet a little wider than your hips, toes turned slightly out.
Reach your arms forward for balance and sit down between your heels.
Go as deep as you can with your heels down and your back flat.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up tall.
commonMistakes: Heels lifting off the floor.
Knees caving inward.
Cutting the depth short.
videoTitle: How To Perform A PERFECT Squat | Squat University

name: Clean and press
steps: Set the bell between your feet. Hinge and grip the handle with one hand.
Hike it back slightly, then drive your hips forward and pull the bell up close to your body into the rack: handle in your palm, bell resting on your forearm, elbow tucked.
Let the bell roll around your hand rather than flipping over and banging your wrist.
From the rack, squeeze your glutes, brace, and press strictly overhead to a locked-out arm.
Lower to the rack, then let the bell drop back between your legs under control. Finish all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep the bell close on the clean, like zipping up a jacket.
Straight wrist, bicep by the ear.
commonMistakes: Swinging the bell wide so it crashes onto the forearm.
Leaning back or bending the knees to push the press.
Bent wrist in the rack.
videoTitle: Kettlebell clean and press | StrongFirst (Short)

name: Renegade row
steps: Get into a push-up position with your hands on the handles of two kettlebells, feet a bit wider than hip-width.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes so your hips stay square to the floor.
Row one bell to your hip while pushing the other hand down into its bell.
Lower it under control and repeat on the other side.
Only one bell? Put one hand on the floor and do all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Push the floor away with the support hand.
commonMistakes: Rotating the hips to lift the bell.
Sagging hips.
Feet too close together, so you tip over.
videoTitle: Kettlebell Renegade Row | Onnit Academy
